modules.title: [MOCK] Welcome to Husky Matchmaker
modules.description: Placeholder overview module explaining what this pilot preview is and is not.
modules.text_content:
This is placeholder content for a hypothetical "Husky Matchmaker" advising pilot, built only to prove out the ADAR guest-learning platform's ability to host a second, separately-configured public course alongside the existing Agomonia Labs Knowledge Academy. No claim in this module is a real University of Washington policy, program, or contact -- it is illustrative copy standing in for content that would need to come from UW's own advising and program staff.

In a real pilot, this module would introduce the program: what "matching" means in this context (for example, connecting a student's stated interests and constraints to majors, minors, certificate programs, or advisors who can speak to them), who the pilot is for, and what a student can expect from an AI Tutor that only answers from curated, UW-approved source material rather than guessing.

Every answer this AI Tutor gives is grounded in whatever documents are attached to this course -- right now, only this placeholder text. Once real program guides, advising FAQs, and major-requirement sheets are supplied, the Tutor's answers will reflect those documents instead.

modules.title: [MOCK] Exploring Majors & Career Pathways
modules.description: Placeholder module on how a student might explore majors and pathways through the pilot.
modules.text_content:
Placeholder content only. In a real version of this module, a student would be able to ask the AI Tutor open-ended questions -- "what majors touch both design and biology," "what's the difference between these two related degrees," "what would a first-generation student want to know before choosing a pathway" -- and get answers grounded in UW's actual program descriptions, course catalogs, and pathway guides, each one citing the specific document it came from.

This mock module stands in for that real content. A generic, illustrative example of the kind of structure real content might follow: an overview of a field of study, the kinds of courses a student in it typically takes, common combinations with other majors or minors, and where to go next (an advising appointment, an info session, a student organization) if the pathway sounds like a fit.

None of the specific majors, requirements, or course numbers a student might ask about are represented here -- they would need to come from UW's own academic departments and be kept current as requirements change.

modules.text_content:
Placeholder content only. A real version of this module would explain, using UW's actual advising structure, how a student is assigned or chooses an advisor, what an advising appointment typically covers, how to prepare questions in advance, and how advising differs across a student's first year versus a declared major.
